editorial.tldr: This page groups items by the shared phrase "large language models"; they do not form one developing story. Oct 9-22 items cover knowledge graphs, sycophancy, code-translation hallucinations, search agents, and spectral edits.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 26 adds a long-horizon web-search benchmark with failure-node localization, a neuron-steering method, self-evolving KG reasoning, and Reva, a real-time vulnerability detector for generated code.
editorial.why_it_matters: Treat this as a reading list, not a thread. For platform engineers the useful items are LongSearchEval (agent failure localization) and Reva (screening agent-written code), plus the code-translation hallucination catalog.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you run coding agents, read Reva and check whether per-function vulnerability screening could sit before review; if you run search agents, try LongSearchEval's failure-node localization on your traces. Skip the rest unless it matches your domain.

open_questions: Does independent replication confirm the spectral-intervention capability shifts?
Do the code-translation mitigations hold on languages outside the paper's test set?
Does Reva's real-time screening keep false positives low enough to gate agent-written code?
Does CANS steering preserve general capability on models beyond those it was tested on?
